verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled for 2026.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1'; R2: 'launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, April 1'; R3: 'successful liftoff... on April 1'; R5: 'Launch: April 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe the mission as having launched and occurred in April 2026, not as future-scheduled; claim's present tense 'is scheduled' contradicts the past completion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a first-crewed flight test of NASA’s Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The first crewed test flight under NASA’s Artemis program'; R2: 'first mission with crew aboard the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R4: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R5: 'first crewed mission of the Artemis programme'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state it is the first crewed flight/test of Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a first-crewed flight test of NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'demonstrating a broad range of SLS and Orion capabilities'; R2: 'first mission with crew aboard the SLS rocket'; R4: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm it as the first crewed SLS flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II has a duration of approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day journey'; R2: '10-day mission'; R4: '10-day mission'; R5: 'Duration: 10 days'; R6: '10-day journey'; R9: 'nearly 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources directly state ~10 days duration.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will carry four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Four Artemis II astronauts are flying aboard NASA’s Orion spacecraft around the Moon and back'; R4: 'orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission'; R5: 'carrying four astronauts on a journey around the Moon and back'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe four astronauts flying around the Moon and back.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will verify all spacecraft systems—including life support—in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test how the spacecraft’s systems operate in a deep space environment'; 'evaluate Orion’s life-support, propulsion, power, thermal, and navigation systems'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to verifying systems including life support in deep space.

verifications.claim: The primary purpose of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems with a crew on board.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The primary goal of Artemis II is a crewed test flight in lunar space'; lists multiple systems including life-support but not as sole primary
verifications.reasoning: Primary purpose is broader crewed test flight; life-support is one of several systems tested, not 'the' primary.

verifications.claim: The primary purpose of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft's navigation systems with a crew on board.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The primary goal of Artemis II is a crewed test flight in lunar space'; navigation is one of multiple systems
verifications.reasoning: Primary purpose is overall crewed test; navigation is included but not primary.

verifications.claim: The primary purpose of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft's propulsion systems with a crew on board.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The primary goal of Artemis II is a crewed test flight in lunar space'; propulsion is one of multiple systems
verifications.reasoning: Primary purpose is crewed test flight; propulsion tested but not 'the' primary.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will take four astronauts on a free-return trajectory around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'free-return trajectory'; R5: 'safe, free-return trajectory'; R9: 'free return trajectory'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm free-return trajectory around Moon with four astronauts.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory reaches up to 252,760 miles from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'reach a maximum distance of 252,760 miles from Earth'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to the specified distance.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory comes within roughly 4,000 miles of the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'pass within 4,070 miles of the lunar surface'; R6: 'coming as close as 4,000 miles'
verifications.reasoning: Exact figures match 'roughly 4,000 miles'.

verifications.claim: Astronauts will manually operate the Orion spacecraft on Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'conduct manual spacecraft operations'; R5: 'astronauts will also take manual control'; R8: 'Victor Glover took manual control'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of manual operations by astronauts.

verifications.claim: Astronauts will test the Orion spacecraft on Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'putting the Orion spacecraft through a series of planned tests'; R2: 'put the Orion spacecraft through planned tests'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state astronauts test Orion systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II involves conducting in-flight human health studies.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'participate in science activities... including... human health studies'; R2: 'human health studies'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit mention of human health studies.

verifications.claim: Artemis II includes crew from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: All sources list NASA and CSA crew members.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and agencies match across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed Artemis mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s first crewed Artemis mission'; R2: 'builds on... Artemis I... uncrewed'; R5: 'first crewed mission of the Artemis programme'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as first crewed Artemis mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17'; R3: 'first humans toward the Moon since 1972'; R4: 'first time since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first beyond LEO since 1972/Apollo 17.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will launch from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R2: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: Consistent launch site confirmation.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will launch on the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'SLS (Space Launch System)'; R3: 'NASA’s SLS rocket'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm SLS launch vehicle.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory includes a translunar injection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'translunar injection burn'; R6: 'translunar injection (TLI)'; R8: 'translunar injection burn'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention translunar injection.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory circles the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lunar flyby'; R6: 'whip around the lunar far side'
verifications.reasoning: Described as circling/flying around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will return for a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'safe splashdown off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean off of the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Confirmed Pacific Ocean splashdown.
